inputs.original_text: The US has put forward a 15-point ceasefire plan through Pakistan, but Iran’s five counter-conditions—demanding an end to aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—show how far apart the sides remain. A ceasefire that rewards force or gives Tehran greater leverage over a vital passage would not secure lasting peace. Israel is right to remain sceptical and to insist it cannot surrender its ability to defend itself against future threats. Any settlement must protect security and stability, not simply pressure one side to accept Iran’s demands.
inputs.modified_text: A ceasefire is not peace if it rewards force and hands Tehran more leverage over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s five counter-conditions make clear how far apart the sides remain, and Israel should not be pressured to give up its ability to defend its people against future threats. The US should stand firm: any settlement must protect security and stability, not legitimize coercion or make a vital passage more vulnerable. Without order and credible defenses, families and nations alike are left exposed.
